subject: ENGLISH
title: Sight-Word Path · M01 D15
objective: Read and use selected high-frequency words in meaningful sentences.
introduction: Some words you just know in a snap: have, said, please, because, there, where. Read them, say them, use them!

vocabulary.definition: A group of words that tells a complete idea, like “I have a book.”
A group of letters with a meaning, like have or said.
A tale with characters and events that can include familiar sight words.

items.explanation: Mina said hello — said is the talking word. “Mina there hello” and “Mina please hello” do not make sense.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses “please” the right way?
items.explanation: In “Please sit there,” please asks kindly and there tells the place. “Please where sit” and “Please because sit” mix up the sight words.

items.prompt: Which word is missing in “I am happy ___ I have a pet”?
items.explanation: Because tells why: I am happy because I have a pet. There tells a place, and please asks kindly.
“I have a pencil” means the pencil is with me. Where asks a place, and because tells why.
“I have a book” shows the book is with me. Where and because are not things you can have.
